dedupe_keys.name: western interconnect transmission line wildfire risk probabilities pnnl wrest outputs

description: This dataset holds wildfire risk probabilities for transmission lines in the Western Interconnection, released by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory on the DOE Data Explorer in January 2026. Lines are identified only by their HIFLD dataset identifier, so users join the probabilities to the HIFLD transmission line layer themselves. The probabilities are generated with PNNL's WREST wildfire risk and resilience tool, using as inputs the HIFLD transmission line data and wildfire burn potentials and flame lengths from PNNL's RADR-FIRE tool for 2025. The record is subject-tagged for public safety power shut-offs and wildfire risk. Coverage is the Western Interconnection of the United States for one input year. Access: DOE Data Explorer record with DOI 10.11578/3018229, free; the page states no licence and does not list the file format. Caveats: identifiers only, no geometry, and the probabilities depend on the 2025 burn potential inputs. It suits wildfire risk screening and shut-off planning for transmission, and relates to the CPUC fire-threat map catalogued here.
